items.q: A zener diode of 12 V carries a current of 50 mA. Calculate the power it dissipates in watts.

items.s: With a midpoint quiescent point the swing either way is Vcc/2 = 4.5 V.

items.q: For an ideal operational amplifier the input resistor is 2 kilohms and the feedback resistor is 100 kilohms. State the magnitude of the closed loop gain of the inverting configuration.
items.s: Magnitude of gain = Rf/Rin = 100/2 = 50.

items.q: Convert the binary number 1010 to its decimal value.
items.s: 1010 in binary is 10 in decimal.

items.q: A gate has a propagation delay of 10 nanoseconds and a signal passes through 20 such gates in cascade. Calculate the total delay in nanoseconds.
items.s: Total delay = 10 x 20 = 200 ns.

items.q: A semiconductor has a carrier concentration of 2e+22 per cubic metre and a mobility of 0.135 square metres per volt second. Calculate its conductivity in siemens per metre.
A material has 8e+22 carriers per cubic metre with a mobility of 0.15 square metres per volt second. Calculate its resistivity in ohm metres.
Calculate the thermal voltage of a junction at a temperature of 350 K, taking Boltzmann constant as 1.38 x 10^-23 J/K and electronic charge as 1.6 x 10^-19 C.
A silicon diode has a reverse saturation current of 2 picoamperes and an ideality factor of 1.5. Calculate its forward current in milliamperes at 0.65 V, taking the thermal voltage as 26 mV.
A small change of 0.02 V across a forward biased diode produces a current change of 2 mA. Calculate its dynamic resistance in ohms.
An LED of forward voltage 0.7 V is to be run at 20 mA from a 24 V supply. Calculate the series resistor required in ohms.
A half wave rectifier is supplied with a sine wave of peak value 24 V. Calculate the direct output voltage in volts.
A full wave rectifier is fed with a sine wave of peak value 20 V. Calculate its direct output voltage in volts.
A full wave rectifier delivers 50 mA to a load with a smoothing capacitor of 1000 microfarads. The supply frequency is 60 Hz. Calculate the peak to peak ripple voltage in volts.
A bridge rectifier is supplied from a transformer secondary of peak voltage 30 V. State the peak inverse voltage each diode must withstand, in volts.
items.s: In a bridge rectifier the peak inverse voltage is equal to the peak secondary voltage, 30 V.

items.q: A centre tapped full wave rectifier has a secondary whose half winding peak voltage is 24 V. State the peak inverse voltage per diode in volts.
items.s: Each diode must withstand twice the half winding peak, that is 48 V.

items.q: A transformer secondary must supply a rectifier whose peak voltage is 30 V. Calculate the required root mean square secondary rating in volts.
A full wave rectifier with a peak input of 20 V has a diode drop of 0.7 V. Calculate the ratio of direct output to peak output as a percentage.
items.s: Direct output = 2 Vm/pi - Vd = 12.03 V against a peak of 12.73 V, giving 94.5%.

items.q: A zener of 5 V is to draw 20 mA from a 24 V supply. Calculate the series resistor required in ohms.
An LED with a forward voltage of 2 V is to pass 10 mA from a 9 V rail. Find the series resistance in ohms.
A transistor has a collector current of 4 mA and a base current of 40 microamperes. Calculate its current gain.
A transistor of current gain 50 carries a collector current of 3 mA. Calculate the base current in microamperes.
items.s: Ib = Ic/beta = 3 x 10^-3/50 = 60 microamperes.

items.q: A transistor of current gain 150 has a collector current of 2 mA. Calculate its emitter current in milliamperes.
items.s: Ie = Ic (beta + 1)/beta = 2 x 151/150 = 2.01 mA.

items.q: A transistor with a collector resistor of 1.5 kilohms draws 2 mA from a 12 V supply. Calculate the collector emitter voltage in volts.
items.s: Vce = Vcc - Ic Rc = 12 - 2 x 1.5 = 9 V.

items.q: A base current of 100 microamperes is required with a base emitter drop of 0.7 V from a 6 V supply. Calculate the base resistor in kilohms.
A change of 0.2 V in gate voltage produces a drain current change of 2 mA. Calculate the transconductance in millisiemens.
items.s: gm = dId/dVgs = 2 x 10^-3/0.2 = 10 mS.

items.q: A field effect stage has a drain resistor of 1 kilohms carrying 3 mA from a 24 V supply. Calculate the drain source voltage in volts.
items.s: Vds = Vdd - Id Rd = 24 - 3 x 1 = 21 V.

items.q: A junction field effect transistor has a saturation current of 8 mA and a pinch off voltage of 4 V. Calculate its drain current in milliamperes when the gate source voltage is -1.5 V.
items.s: Id = Idss (1 - Vgs/Vp) squared = 8 x (1 - 1.5/4) squared = 3.12 mA.

items.q: An amplifier delivers an output of 2 V from an input of 10 mV. Calculate its voltage gain.
An amplifier has a voltage gain of 100. Express this gain in decibels.
items.s: Gain in dB = 20 log(Av) = 20 log(100) = 40 dB.

items.q: An amplifier is rated with a voltage gain of 40 dB. Calculate its numerical voltage gain.
items.s: Av = 10 raised to the power of (dB/20) = 10^(40/20) = 100.

items.q: An amplifier accepts 20 mW and delivers 1 W. Calculate its power gain.
items.s: Power gain = Pout/Pin = 1/(20 x 10^-3) = 50.

items.q: A coupling network uses a 1 kilohm resistor and a 1 microfarad capacitor. Calculate its cut off frequency in hertz.
An amplifier of open loop gain 5000 uses negative feedback with a feedback fraction of 0.01. Calculate the closed loop gain.

An inverting amplifier of input resistor 2 kilohms and feedback resistor 20 kilohms is fed with 0.2 V. Calculate the output voltage in volts.
items.s: Vout = -(Rf/Rin) Vin = -(20/2) x 0.2 = -2 V.

items.q: A summing amplifier has two equal input resistors of 10 kilohms and a feedback resistor of 20 kilohms. Its inputs are 1 V and 0.25 V. Calculate the output voltage in volts.

items.q: An output can source 8 mA while each input requires 0.8 mA. Calculate the fan out of the gate.
